Management Insights & Variations

Data-supported interpretation of targets, trends, drivers and areas requiring attention
Executive takeaway3Mixed
  • Priority concern: Execution gap: Audits Completed were 10 against 23 Audits Planned in the latest period. The completion-to-plan ratio was 43.5%, leaving 13 planned audits uncompleted. Review basis: validate against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
  • Favourable development: Severity mix became more favourable: High Risk Findings as a share of Audit Findings fell from 24.0% to 2.9%. This is a data-supported mix change, not proof of the underlying cause. Review basis: validate against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
  • Key context: Planning versus completion: the prior period recorded 17 completed against 11 planned, while the latest period recorded 10 against 23. Because planned and completed counts may relate to different audit cohorts, the prior-period ratio is shown descriptively rather than treated as a directly comparable execution rate.
What is going well2
  • Severity mix became more favourable: High Risk Findings as a share of Audit Findings fell from 24.0% to 2.9%. This is a data-supported mix change, not proof of the underlying cause. Review basis: validate against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
  • Resolution activity improved: Findings Resolved increased from 6 to 7 (16.7%). This indicates higher closure activity; assess it alongside new findings and the outstanding backlog. Review basis: validate against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
Variations requiring attention3
  • Execution gap: Audits Completed were 10 against 23 Audits Planned in the latest period. The completion-to-plan ratio was 43.5%, leaving 13 planned audits uncompleted. Review basis: validate against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
  • Resolution coverage weakened: resolved findings relative to total findings fell from 24.0% to 20.6%. Review basis: validate against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
  • Audits Completed decreased from 17 to 10 (-41.2%). This movement is adverse based on the KPI direction available in the data. Management review: review the movement against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver before drawing a causal conclusion.
Contextual movements — review, do not pre-classify5
  • Audits Planned increased from 11 to 23 (109.1%). This is a contextual movement; assess it against capacity, target, case mix, operating range or the actual business outcome before calling it favourable or adverse. Management review: validate against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
  • Audit Findings increased from 25 to 34 (36.0%). This is a contextual movement; assess it against capacity, target, case mix, operating range or the actual business outcome before calling it favourable or adverse. Management review: validate against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
  • High Risk Findings decreased from 6 to 1 (-83.3%). This is a contextual movement; assess it against capacity, target, case mix, operating range or the actual business outcome before calling it favourable or adverse. Management review: validate against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
  • Open Findings decreased from 33 to 21 (-36.4%). This is a contextual movement; assess it against capacity, target, case mix, operating range or the actual business outcome before calling it favourable or adverse. Management review: validate against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
  • Repeat Findings decreased from 9 to 6 (-33.3%). This is a contextual movement; assess it against capacity, target, case mix, operating range or the actual business outcome before calling it favourable or adverse. Management review: validate against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
Management interpretation & possible drivers2
  • Management interpretation: the principal movements above should be read together rather than in isolation. Review the largest movement with its supporting volume, mix, quality or productivity indicators before attributing a cause.
  • Possible driver review: compare the leading movement with the next supporting KPI(s) and the comparable period to determine whether the change is broad-based or concentrated.
Key relationships & derived ratios4
  • Planning versus completion: the prior period recorded 17 completed against 11 planned, while the latest period recorded 10 against 23. Because planned and completed counts may relate to different audit cohorts, the prior-period ratio is shown descriptively rather than treated as a directly comparable execution rate.
  • Findings intensity: findings per completed audit moved from 1.47 to 3.4 (131.2%). This derived ratio should be read with audit coverage and audit scope before drawing conclusions about control quality.
  • High-risk share: High Risk Findings represented 2.9% of Audit Findings in the latest period, compared with 24.0% previously.
  • Backlog versus closure: open findings moved from 33 to 21, while resolved findings moved from 6 to 7. The combined movement should be reviewed to distinguish new inflow from effective remediation.
Management action5
  • Execution gap:: Validate the movement with the responsible business owner against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
  • Resolution coverage weakened:: Validate the movement with the responsible business owner against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
  • Audits Completed: Validate the movement with the responsible business owner against the closest supporting KPI, target or operating driver.
  • Review the derived ratios and KPI relationships before assessing individual movements; they provide context but do not establish causation.
  • Record the agreed corrective or sustaining action, responsible owner and review date where a material variance requires follow-up.
